Built with Java, it provides over 2,000 [plugins](https://plugins.jenkins.io/) to support automating virtually anything, so that humans can spend their time doing things machines cannot. # What to Use Jenkins for and When to Use It Use Jenkins to automate your development workflow, so you can focus on work that matters most. Jenkins is commonly used for: - Building projects - Running tests to detect bugs and other issues as soon as they are introduced - Static code analysis - Deployment Execute repetitive tasks, save time, and optimize your development process with Jenkins. # Downloads The Jenkins project provides official distributions as WAR files, Docker images, native packages and installers for platforms including several Linux distributions and Windows. See the [Downloads](https://www.jenkins.io/download) page for references. For all distributions Jenkins offers two release lines: - [Weekly](https://www.jenkins.io/download/weekly/) - Frequent releases which include all new features, improvements, and bug fixes. - [Long-Term Support (LTS)](https://www.jenkins.io/download/lts/) - Older release line which gets periodically updated via bug fix backports. Latest releases: # Getting Started (Development) For more information on setting up your development environment, contributing, and working with Jenkins internals, check the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Jenkins Developer Documentation](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/developer/). # Source Our latest and greatest source of Jenkins can be found on [GitHub](https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins). Fork us! # Contributing to Jenkins New to open source or Jenkins? Here’s how to get started: - Read the [Contribution Guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) - Check our [good first issues](https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3A%22good%20first%20issue%22) - Join our [Gitter chat](https://matrix.to/#/#jenkinsci_newcomer-contributors:gitter.im) for questions and help For more information about participating in the community and contributing to the Jenkins project, see [this page](https://www.jenkins.io/participate/). Documentation for Jenkins core maintainers is in the [maintainers guidelines](docs/MAINTAINERS.adoc). # News and Website All information about Jenkins can be found on our [official website](https://www.jenkins.io/), including documentation, blog posts, plugin listings, community updates, and more. Stay up-to-date with the latest Jenkins news, tutorials, and release notes: - [Jenkins Blog](https://www.jenkins.io/blog/) - [Documentation](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/) - [Plugins Index](https://plugins.jenkins.io/) - [Events](https://www.jenkins.io/events/) Follow Jenkins on social media to stay connected with the community: - [Twitter / X](https://x.com/jenkinsci) - [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@jenkinscicd) - [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/jenkins-project/) # Governance The Jenkins project is governed by an open source community. To learn more about the governance structure, project leadership, and how decisions are made, visit the [Governance Page](https://www.jenkins.io/project/governance/). # Adopters Jenkins is trusted by **millions of users** and adopted by **thousands of companies** around the world — from startups to enterprises — to automate their software delivery pipelines. Explore the [Adopters Page](https://www.jenkins.io/project/adopters/) and https://stories.jenkins.io to see: - Companies and organizations using Jenkins - Success stories and case studies - How Jenkins is used in different industries > If your company uses Jenkins and you'd like to be featured, feel free to [submit your story](https://www.jenkins.io/project/adopters/contributing/#share-your-story)! # License Jenkins is **licensed** under the **[MIT License](LICENSE.txt)**.

aiSummary.oneLiner: The leading open-source automation server for building, deploying, and automating software projects.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Jenkins is a robust, extensible automation server built in Java that serves as the backbone for Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines worldwide. It automates the repetitive tasks of software development, such as building code, running tests, and deploying applications to various environments. With an ecosystem of over 2,000 plugins, Jenkins can integrate with virtually any tool in the CI/CD toolchain. It allows teams to define complex deployment pipelines as code, ensuring reliable, repeatable, and scalable software delivery processes. It is a critical piece of infrastructure for thousands of organizations, from startups to large enterprises.
keyFeatures: Massive Plugin Ecosystem: Supports over 2,000 plugins, enabling integration with almost every version control, build, and deployment tool available.
Pipelines as Code: Allows developers to define complex CI/CD workflows using Groovy-based Jenkinsfiles stored directly alongside application code.
Distributed Builds: Scales effortlessly by distributing build and test workloads across multiple agent machines and platforms.
Extensive Platform Support: Offers official distributions for Windows, macOS, various Linux flavors, and Docker containers.
Community Governed: Driven by a massive open-source community that ensures continuous updates, long-term support releases, and extensive documentation.

useCases.title: Continuous Integration
useCases.description: Automatically triggering builds and running test suites every time code is committed to a repository to catch bugs early.

useCases.title: Automated Deployment
useCases.description: Orchestrating the complex process of pushing validated code through staging environments and into production.

useCases.title: Static Code Analysis
useCases.description: Integrating with code quality tools to automatically scan codebases for vulnerabilities and style violations during the build process.

useCases.title: Task Automation
useCases.description: Scheduling and running arbitrary batch jobs, database backups, or infrastructure provisioning scripts.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Jenkins is an essential tool for DevOps engineers, software developers, and system administrators tasked with automating and managing software delivery pipelines at any scale. The platform simplifies complex workflows and accelerates development timelines.

_This is an automatically generated changelog draft for Jenkins weekly releases.
See https://www.jenkins.io/changelog/2.590/ for the official changelog for this release._

## 🚨 Removed

* Remove up-for-adoption source code management plugins from wizard (#26617) @StefanSpieker

## 🚀 New features and improvements

* Make the side panel collapsible on mobile (#27709) @janfaracik
* Refine page frame and experimental UI on mobile (#27708) @janfaracik
* Stop using progressive rendering for build history (#27636) @timja, @claude

## 🐛 Bug fixes

* Highlight build tab while one of its subpages is shown (#27697) @uhafner, @claude
* Fix offline-node -m usage text: the command takes the node offline, does not disconnect it (#27656) @NUAAwqy
* Fix CLI usage text: connect-node and disconnect-node do not support comma-separated lists (#27655) @NUAAwqy
* Fix synchronization markers spanning output writes (#27592) @Rauneet-coder
* Ignore stale autocomplete suggestions after input changes or focus leaves (#27504) @thswlsqls

## 👷 Changes for plugin developers

* Deprecated `AbstractTopLevelItem` (#27584) @jglick

All contributors: @janfaracik, @jglick, @NUAAwqy, @Raune

releases.body:
Please report any issues found to the [release candidate announcement thread](https://groups.google.com/g/jenkinsci-dev/c/gy2EX2FE_u8/m/-sH8jeXiBwAJ).

The final release is scheduled for **November 25th, 2026**.

Download the release from the [artifact repository](https://repo.jenkins-ci.org/incrementals/org/jenkins-ci/main/jenkins-war/2.580.3-rc38649.1f9a_6fe70721/jenkins-war-2.580.3-rc38649.1f9a_6fe70721.war). 

After the final release, the [official changelog](https://www.jenkins.io/changelog/2.580.3/) and [official upgrade guide](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/upgrade-guide/2.580/#upgrading-to-jenkins-lts-2-580-3) will be available on [www.jenkins.io/download](http://www.jenkins.io/download).

_This is an automatically generated changelog draft for Jenkins weekly releases.
See https://www.jenkins.io/changelog/2.589/ for the official changelog for this release._

## 🚀 New features and improvements

* Convert six Groovy configuration views to Jelly (#27644) @timja, @claude
* [JENKINS-70822](https://issue-redirect.jenkins.io/issue/70822) - Improve plugin manager search (#9137) @timja
* Extend Experimental Job UI Builds list with plugin support (#27508) @janfaracik

All contributors: @janfaracik, @timja, and @claude

_This is an automatically generated changelog draft for Jenkins weekly releases.
See https://www.jenkins.io/changelog/2.588/ for the official changelog for this release._

## 🔒  Security

Multiple security fixes. See the [2026-10-28 security advisory](https://www.jenkins.io/security/advisory/2026-10-28/) for details.

We're excited to announce the release of Jenkins 2.580.2 🎉 

## Changelog and upgrade guide

See the [changelog](https://www.jenkins.io/changelog-stable/#v2.580.2) and [upgrade guide](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/upgrade-guide/2.580/#upgrading-to-jenkins-lts-2-580-2) to learn about breaking changes and other considerations when updating.

## Reporting issues

If you find an issue with this release, please file an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins/issues), otherwise use the [forums](https://community.jenkins.io/) if you're unsure whether you encounter an issue or not.

Table of Contents

  • About

About

In a nutshell, Jenkins is the leading open-source automation server. Built with Java, it provides over 2,000 plugins to support automating virtually anything, so that humans can spend their time doing things machines cannot.

What to Use Jenkins for and When to Use It

Use Jenkins to automate your development workflow, so you can focus on work that matters most. Jenkins is commonly used for:

  • Building projects
  • Running tests to detect bugs and other issues as soon as they are introduced
  • Static code analysis
  • Deployment

Execute repetitive tasks, save time, and optimize your development process with Jenkins.

Downloads

The Jenkins project provides official distributions as WAR files, Docker images, native packages and installers for platforms including several Linux distributions and Windows. See the Downloads page for references.

For all distributions Jenkins offers two release lines:

  • Weekly - Frequent releases which include all new features, improvements, and bug fixes.
  • Long-Term Support (LTS) - Older release line which gets periodically updated via bug fix backports.

Latest releases:

Getting Started (Development)

For more information on setting up your development environment, contributing, and working with Jenkins internals, check the contributing guide and the Jenkins Developer Documentation.

Source

Our latest and greatest source of Jenkins can be found on GitHub. Fork us!

Contributing to Jenkins

New to open source or Jenkins? Here’s how to get started:

  • Read the Contribution Guidelines
  • Check our good first issues
  • Join our Gitter chat for questions and help

For more information about participating in the community and contributing to the Jenkins project, see this page.

Documentation for Jenkins core maintainers is in the maintainers guidelines.

News and Website

All information about Jenkins can be found on our official website, including documentation, blog posts, plugin listings, community updates, and more.

Stay up-to-date with the latest Jenkins news, tutorials, and release notes:

  • Jenkins Blog
  • Documentation
  • Plugins Index
  • Events

Follow Jenkins on social media to stay connected with the community:

  • Twitter / X
  • YouTube
  • LinkedIn

Governance

The Jenkins project is governed by an open source community. To learn more about the governance structure, project leadership, and how decisions are made, visit the Governance Page.

Adopters

Jenkins is trusted by millions of users and adopted by thousands of companies around the world — from startups to enterprises — to automate their software delivery pipelines.

Explore the Adopters Page and https://stories.jenkins.io to see:

  • Companies and organizations using Jenkins
  • Success stories and case studies
  • How Jenkins is used in different industries

If your company uses Jenkins and you'd like to be featured, feel free to submit your story!

License

Jenkins is licensed under the MIT License.
